rounds.proof_sketch: For dim=1 reduction with input shape [16, 256, 256]: block_size = min(dim2, 1024) = min(256, 1024) = 256. Thread indices threadIdx.x range from 0 to 255. In the kernel, col = threadIdx.x, so col ∈ [0, 255]. The mutation changes 'col >= dim2' (col >= 256) to 'col > dim2' (col > 256). Since col is always in [0, 255], both conditions are always FALSE for all threads. No thread ever returns early in either version, making the mutation semantically invisible.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary guard from 'col >= dim2' to 'col > dim2' in min_reduction_dim1_kernel. This would only cause different behavior when col == dim2 (i.e., col == 256). However, the kernel launch configuration sets block_size = min(dim2, 1024) = 256, meaning exactly 256 threads are launched per block with threadIdx.x values 0-255. Since col = threadIdx.x, the value col = 256 is impossible to achieve. Both the original condition (256 >= 256 = true) and mutated condition (256 > 256 = false) are never evaluated with col == 256. With col always in [0, 255], both 'col >= 256' and 'col > 256' are always false, meaning no thread ever takes the early-return path in either version. The mutation is semantically equivalent under the fixed shape configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE under fixed-shape contract. The mutation would only matter if col == dim2 were reachable, which requires either: (1) dim2 > 1024 so block_size < dim2 and threads with indices >= dim2 exist but should be masked, or (2) block_size explicitly set larger than dim2. Neither is possible with fixed shape [16, 256, 256] where dim2 = 256 and block_size = 256.
rounds.recommendations: When testing CUDA kernel boundary guards, the testing framework should verify whether the boundary condition is actually reachable given the fixed launch configuration. For mutations on guards like 'idx >= N', check if the maximum possible idx value equals N or exceeds N. If max(idx) = N-1 (as happens when block_size = N), mutations to the guard are equivalent. Consider adding shape-aware mutation filtering to avoid generating unreachable boundary mutations.
